extracted.intended_audience: general readers, comics creators, and scholars interested in comics theory and practice
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography of comics theorist and cartoonist Scott McCloud that summarizes his creative work, theories (Understanding Comics, Making Comics, Reinventing Comics), and contributions such as the 24-hour comic and Creator's Bill of Rights. Useful as a pointer to practices and production constraints in comics creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24-hour comic
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete 24-page comic created by a single cartoonist in 24 consecutive hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coined by McCloud in 1990 as a mutual challenge (with Steve Bissette) intended to compel creative output with a minimum of self-restraining contemplation. Thousands of cartoonists have since taken up the challenge (examples include Neil Gaiman, Kevin Eastman, Dave Sim, Rick Veitch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator's Bill of Rights (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1988 document with the stated aim of protecting the rights of comic book creators and helping aid against the exploitation of comic artists and writers by corporate work-for-hire practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCloud was the principal author; the Bill was adopted by a group of artists (e.g., Kevin Eastman, Dave Sim, Stephen R. Bissette). It contains twelve rights intended to assert creators' control and protections over their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to full ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: "The right to full ownership of what we fully create."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted as one of the twelve rights in the Creator's Bill of Rights — presented as a core entitlement creators should claim to avoid exploitation under work-for-hire arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to prompt payment of fair share
rubrics_metrics.description: "The right to prompt payment of a fair and equitable share of profits derived from all of our creative work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted as one of the twelve rights in the Creator's Bill of Rights — emphasizes timely and equitable compensation as a standard for creator treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinite canvas (digital layout technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'infinite canvas' permitted by a web browser, allowing panels to be spatially arranged in ways not possible in the finite, two-dimensional, paged format of a physical book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCloud explores this technique as one of the ways web technology enables new comics layouts and storytelling possibilities distinct from traditional page-based comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making Comics (instructional approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: An instructional guide to the process of producing comics that presents 'storytelling secrets of comics, manga, and graphic novels.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a practical instructional book (Making Comics, 2006) that aims to teach the process of producing comics; the Wikipedia page notes McCloud toured giving lectures to promote these principles. The page does not enumerate the book's specific rules here, but positions it as a how-to resource on craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinventing Comics (advocacy for 'revolutions')
rubrics_metrics.description: A book (Reinventing Comics, 2000) in which McCloud outlined twelve 'revolutions' he argued would be keys to the growth and success of comics as a popular and creative medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references the book's framing of technological and systemic changes (the 'revolutions') as criteria/conditions for future success of the medium, though the article does not list the twelve revolutions verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micropayments as a digital monetization strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy for micropayments as a model to support web-based comics distribution and creator compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCloud was an early advocate and adviser to BitPass, and he experimented with pricing an online graphic novella in small increments (The Right Number). Presented on the page as a suggested business/monetization practice for web delivery of comics.
